# Requirements Document: Removing a service from a bundle

## Introduction

A bundle is sold at one price.  In the seat worked example one order item at
1,000.00 EUR holds both passengers' flights and bags, and the cancellation page
removes a passenger by cancelling that passenger's services inside such an
item.  The guide prices a bundle only as a whole and does not say how much of
the price belongs to one of its services.  The model takes the share as a
parameter, a reading of the sources.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Bundle.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Bundle.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-607

**User Story:** As a customer who drops one passenger from a bundled trip, I want back the part of the price that passenger's services were worth, so that I pay only for what I keep.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller removes services from a bundle THE SYSTEM SHALL cancel them and return their share of the bundle price under the reading. (Lean: `removeFromBundle`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN services are removed from a bundle THE SYSTEM SHALL mark each named live service that the delivery status table lets be removed CANCELLED with delivery status REMOVED and leave the bundle's other services and its price as they were.
   - ONE-607.1, proven: proven theorem `bundle_removes`; example `bundleAfterRemoval`
2. WHEN services are removed from a bundle THE SYSTEM SHALL return the sum of the shares of the services it cancels under the reading, in the bundle's currency.
   - ONE-607.2, proven: proven theorem `bundle_returns_shares`; example `bundleShares`
3. WHEN services are removed from a bundle THE SYSTEM SHALL return no more than the bundle price.
   - ONE-607.3, open: open theorem `bundle_return_le_price`; counterexample `bundleShares`
4. WHEN every service of a bundle is removed THE SYSTEM SHALL return the whole bundle price.
   - ONE-607.4, open: open theorem `bundle_return_all`; counterexample `bundleShares`

#### Open question on ONE-607.3

> An accepted removal returns no more than the bundle price, under every
> reading.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide prices a bundle only as a whole.
> Under a reading that gives each service its stand-alone price, a 1,000.00 EUR
> bundle of two flights at 470.00 EUR and two bags at 60.00 EUR returns
> 1,060.00 EUR when every service is removed.  The example
> `bundleShares` shows it.  How does a bundle price split among its
> services: by stated component prices, by stand-alone prices, or not at
> all?

#### Open question on ONE-607.4

> Removing every service of a bundle, all of them live, returns the whole
> bundle price, under every reading.
>
> Open question for the business.  Under a reading that gives no share to any
> service, removing a passenger's flight and bag from a 1,000.00 EUR bundle
> returns nothing, and so does removing every service.  The example
> `bundleShares` shows it.  Does removing part of a bundle return part of
> its price, and does removing all of it return all of it?
